headline: The Hormuz premium started leaving overnight on Iran-Oman corridor talks, hours before core PCE, a $70bn 5-year and Nvidia.
stance: Brent $85.98, -2.9% (~6am ET), WTI under $80, on reports of a temporary joint maritime corridor through the strait. That gives back more than half of the premium built since August 4, and most of it in three sessions.

news.head: Iran and Oman talk a temporary Hormuz corridor
news.body: Pakistan's military leadership is in Tehran backing the negotiation and Qatar is still mediating. Crude never actually stopped moving through the strait.

news.head: The 2-year auction stopped through
news.body: $69bn cleared at 4.204% against a 4.208% when-issued. Indirects took 66.0% versus a 56.9% average; primary dealers were left with 10.9%.

news.head: Nvidia reports after today's close
news.body: Street consensus is $92.18bn of revenue and $2.09 adjusted EPS. Company guidance for the quarter was $91bn and $2.04, below the street going in.

implications: A corridor removes freight and insurance cost, not barrels. Nothing about Iran's export capacity changed overnight; what changed is what it costs to move a cargo past it.
The September strip prices 38% odds of a hike this morning against 42% yesterday. Oil moved that, not labor data, and one denial out of Tehran moves it back.

watch.head: Core PCE, Q2 GDP and durable goods, 8:30am ET
watch.body: Consensus looks for 0.2% on core month over month, 3.3% year over year, headline 0.1%. It covers July, so the oil break is not in it.

watch.head: $70bn 5-year note auction, 1pm ET
watch.body: Second of three coupons. Dealer takedown is the tell on whether yesterday's bid was for the front end alone or for duration generally.

watch.head: Nvidia's October guide, after the close
watch.body: The quarter being reported ended July 26. What reprices the complex is the outlook given for the current one, not the number just printed.

watch.head: Hormuz headlines, all session
watch.body: This is talks, not a signed arrangement. Any denial out of Tehran puts the premium straight back into the freight rate and the barrel.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: The front end did the work for the first time this week, and it out-rallied the long end. The whole move was real yields, with breakevens flat into the inflation print.
Foreign accounts paid for that, not dealers. A real bid arriving into a spec long already pinned at the top of its three-year range is not an auction concession.
sections.positioning: New this week: spec net long Swiss franc at the 88th %ile of three years, ten points higher in a week. That haven length was built before the corridor talks surfaced.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: The index closed Tuesday within three points of where it closed Friday. Nobody positioned into this print; they parked.
S&P futures -0.1%, Nasdaq 100 -0.2%, Dow +0.1% (~4am ET). The spread between them is the story: index risk this session is dated tonight, not 8:30.
sections.positioning: Spec net long S&P 500 came off five points on the week to the 86th %ile of three years, the biggest equity shift on the tape and still the wrong side of a bad number.

single_name.note: Prenetics - new to the screen today on an Aug 24 insider filing, above its 200-day, 3.2 days to cover. Two rules fired on a first appearance, which is unusual.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: Every coupon this week settles Monday, 2s, 5s and 7s on the same date, with a $28bn floater landing Friday first. Reserves take all of it.
Funding goes into that calm. Overnight spreads and the commercial paper premium are both at the tight end of the summer, so the drain starts from a comfortable base.
sections.positioning: Primary-dealer high-yield inventory rose eight points on the week to the 12th %ile of three years. Light, but rebuilding into a week that asks the balance sheet for a lot.

single_name.note: UMH Properties - insider buy filed Aug 20, above its 200-day, 7.9 days to cover. A manufactured-housing REIT is a cap-rate trade, and cap rates take the 10-year.
